title: Attack by Stratagem
sourceOrigin: Project Gutenberg eBook #17405, Lionel Giles translation, 1910

approvedQuoteLedger.text: Supreme excellence consists in breaking the enemy's resistance without fighting.
approvedQuoteLedger.sourceLocation: Ch III, sentence 2 (paraphrased form of 'supreme excellence')

approvedQuoteLedger.text: The worst policy of all is to besiege walled cities.
If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles.

structureSummary.part1: sentences 1-2: the hierarchy of outcomes (capture intact beats destroy; victory without fighting beats winning by fighting)
structureSummary.part2: sentences 3-7: the hierarchy of methods (break enemy plans > disrupt alliances > field battle > siege is worst)
structureSummary.part3: sentences 8-10: force ratio rules for engagement, avoidance, and retreat
structureSummary.part4: sentences 11-16: civilian interference as a self-inflicted disaster

usageRules: This sidecar supports brief and outline only. Only three approved quotes may be near-quoted in reader-facing prose.
